outlier.evidence: The only rating above 6: a 7 at confidence 5, the level that says the math and details were checked carefully. The main review is two sentences: 'I think the method this paper proposes is novel, and increamental improvements are explained in detail. Therefore I am giving it an accept.' It calls the work a lidar detection model, describes a 'lidar/camera' task the paper does not have, and never joins the discussion. Without it A still averages 6.0, so it did not decide the outcome.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: Two-sentence main review at confidence 5 with no question or criticism. The summary reduces the paper to lidar detection and ignores the segmentation tasks; the limitations call it a 'lidar/camera detection task/model'. No reply after the authors' thank-you.

checkable_claims.claim: Polar sectors are more efficient than cartesian rectangles, and PolarStream improves 'accuracy and efficiency over existing streaming methods'.
checkable_claims.evidence: The efficiency part is not supported. Figure 1 (right) puts PolarStream within about 2 ms of the cartesian Han et al. at every sector count, and lines 284-286 say STROBE is fastest at 1, 2 and 4 sectors. Table 2 gives 44.9 ms polar against 44.5 ms cartesian. The paper reports no memory figure. The accuracy part holds: PolarStream has the higher PQ at each latency.

checkable_claims.claim: In Figure 5 the method is faster than full-sweep methods but lags them in accuracy.
checkable_claims.evidence: Figure 5: PLS1 and PLS4 reach about 53 mAP against about 60 for CenterPoint, and about 73.5 mIoU against about 78 for AF2S3Net. They lead only in panoptic quality (val split), 69.2 and 68.4 against about 67.7 for PaP.

checkable_claims.claim: The relation and distinction to cylindrical, spherical and hybrid methods [1,15,36,37,38,40] are not discussed.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 2.1 (lines 85-91) describes [1], [38], CVCNet, PolarNet, Cylinder3D and Panoptic-PolarNet. Lines 44-51 state the gap the paper targets: polar grids lag cartesian grids in detection because of distortion. [15] is PointPillars, a cartesian method. The discussion is brief but present.

checkable_claims.claim: The Table 1 baselines are the authors' own implementations and were never validated on the original datasets.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 233-237: Han et al. and STROBE released no code. The authors re-implemented both on nuScenes with their own backbone and input size, and dropped STROBE's HD-map branch. No comparison with the original papers' numbers appears.

checkable_claims.claim: PolarStream shows almost no accuracy loss at 32 sectors.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1, bidirectional padding at n=32 against full sweep: mAP 51.0 vs 51.2, mIoU 72.9 vs 73.7. PQ does drop, 69.2 to 59.1. The rebuttal adds that the n=32 mAP came from an unfinished training run (52.8 when finished).

checkable_claims.claim: Feature undistortion and range stratification help polar pillars but not cartesian pillars, so the gain is not a parameter-count confound.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 2: polar detection mAP 48.2 to 50.3 with both modules; cartesian 50.6 to 50.6.

rebuttal.evidence: Author responses 2021-08-09 and 2021-08-10. Reviewer_88yB replied on 2021-08-31 and edited the review the same day, moving 'from below acceptance threshold to above' (final 6). Reviewer_2ez1 ('positive towards the acceptance', 2021-08-12) and Reviewer_ijm6 ('positive on acceptance', 2021-08-21) kept 6; 2ez1's only edit is on its posting day. Reviewer_8rdp did not respond.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The pledge to release the streaming nuScenes benchmark, the reimplemented baselines and the code. Reviewer_ijm6 called it a 'good citizenship' bonus. Reviewer_88yB cited that phrase and the 'non-availability of open baseline implementations' as its reason to raise. ijm6 also accepted the heavier-backbone table (56.2 mAP vs CenterPoint 56.4; 76.8 mIoU vs Cylinder3D 76.1, val) as showing that the gap to full-sweep methods comes from the backbone. 88yB's question on independent object motion in bidirectional padding went unanswered, and 88yB did not pursue it.

ac.evidence: Two sentences: '4 expert reviewers suggest acceptance after rebuttal', and the paper 'is promised to provide an open benchmark and codebase'. The second point comes from the rebuttal via Reviewer_ijm6 and Reviewer_88yB. 'Expert' overstates the panel: two reviewers chose confidence 3 ('Math/other details were not carefully checked') and Reviewer_8rdp wrote two sentences. No technical point is discussed.

main_reasons_for_decision: All four reviewers rated at or above threshold after the rebuttal (6, 7, 6, 6)
Gains over the streaming baselines in Table 1, clearest in PQ and mIoU
Promised release of an open streaming benchmark, baselines and code ('good citizenship')
Rebuttal attributed the gap to full-sweep methods to backbone size

outlier.evidence: All three rated 5 (marginally below threshold), at confidence 4 or 5, after 4 hours each.

checkable_claims.claim: The cartesian model has almost the same measured latency as the polar model (Table 2 and Figure 1).
checkable_claims.evidence: Figure 1 (right): PolarStream is within about 2 ms of the cartesian Han et al. at every sector count. Table 2: 44.9 ms polar vs 44.5 ms cartesian, but there both inputs are 512x512 by design (line 209), so only Figure 1 bears on the sector claim. The authors' rebuttal table shows larger cartesian feature maps only at 8 or more sectors, and they concede no 'noticeable improvement in runtime' on a V100.

checkable_claims.claim: The polar model has 1-2 mAP lower detection than the cartesian model.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 2: 51.2 vs 52.3 (full sweep). Table 1 without padding: -1.1 (n=1), -2.0 (n=4), -2.5 (n=32). With bidirectional padding polar leads at n=8, 16, 32 (+3.0, +1.4, +1.9). Lines 327-328 concede that polar pillars are 'less accurate in object detection'.

checkable_claims.claim: Figure 1 claims polar is better than cartesian in memory and computation, but no such comparison is provided.
checkable_claims.evidence: The Figure 1 caption says cartesian sectors waste 'half of memory and computation'. The paper reports no memory figure, and its only compute measure, latency, shows near parity. A memory table first appears in the rebuttal: canvas memory differs only at n of 8 or more (2.1 vs 1.3 MB per sector at n=32).

checkable_claims.claim: Detection with 4 or fewer sectors is worse than cartesian, even with context padding.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1 mAP: n=1 51.2 vs 52.3; n=2 51.9 vs 52.2; n=4 53.2 vs 54.9. Lines 250-251 admit it. Cartesian pillars at n=4 (54.9) is the best detector in Table 1.

checkable_claims.claim: Range Stratified Convolution is unclear about how kernels are allocated, and ablations are needed.
checkable_claims.evidence: The main text never states the number or bounds of the strata; Figure 2 shows three as an example and the rebuttal gives eight. Table 2 ablates only the combined module (+0.9 mAP). The stratum-count and conv-versus-norm ablations first appear in the rebuttal.

checkable_claims.claim: Figure 5 shows the method behind in detection and semantic segmentation but state of the art in panoptic segmentation.
checkable_claims.evidence: Figure 5: PLS1 and PLS4 reach about 53 mAP against about 60 for CenterPoint, and about 73.5 mIoU against about 78 for AF2S3Net. They lead only in panoptic quality (val split), 69.2 and 68.4 against about 67.7 for PaP.

rebuttal.evidence: Author responses 2021-08-09 and 2021-08-10. Each review was later edited to add a post-rebuttal note that keeps 5: Reviewer_dNFe 2021-08-22 ('I will keep my original score'), Reviewer_X4zp 2021-09-01 ('My score remains the same'), Reviewer_1vpo 2021-09-06 ('I am thus confirming my initial rating'). No B reviewer replied in the thread.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The feature-map and memory tables did not convince. The authors conceded no runtime gain on a V100 and argued, without measurement, that embedded hardware such as FPGAs would show one. Reviewer_dNFe then asked for a test on an edge device (Jetson AGX Xavier), after the authors' last post. Reviewer_X4zp stayed unconvinced on the memory and compute advantage and on the gain over cartesian coordinates, and called the stratified convolution 'still vague' despite the new stratum ablation. Reviewer_1vpo adopted X4zp's polar concern and claimed readability issues were 'raised across all reviewers', though dNFe called the paper well-written. The heavier-backbone table, also sent to A, did not move dNFe. The statement 'Our major contribution is not polar representation' undercut the paper's first listed contribution.

ac.evidence: The meta-review names 'the justification of polar coordinates' as the most critical concern the response did not address. That is Reviewer_dNFe's lead point, shared by Reviewer_X4zp and adopted by Reviewer_1vpo. It adds 'novelty, writing and experiments' and ends 'I concur'. All three reviewers kept 5.

main_reasons_for_decision: The claim that polar sectors save compute and memory is not supported by the paper's own latency results
Polar detection trails cartesian pillars at full sweep and at 4 or fewer sectors
Incremental novelty over Han et al. and STROBE
Unclear writing, notably Range Stratified Convolution

issues_only_a: Baselines are reimplementations never checked against the original papers' numbers (Reviewer_88yB, Reviewer_ijm6); the rebuttal answered with a pledge to release the benchmark and code
Batch-size-1 latency per sector count and data-loading time for 10-sweep input (Reviewer_2ez1)
Independent object motion in bidirectional padding (Reviewer_88yB); the authors did not answer
Relation to other cylindrical and spherical methods (Reviewer_88yB); Section 2.1 and lines 44-51 cover it briefly
Venue fit: CVPR/ECCV/ICCV or IV may suit better (Reviewer_ijm6)
issues_only_b: Polar sectors show no measured memory or latency saving over cartesian sectors (Reviewer_dNFe, Reviewer_X4zp)
Polar detection trails cartesian at full sweep and at 4 or fewer sectors (Reviewer_dNFe, Reviewer_X4zp)
Range Stratified Convolution&Normalization underspecified: stratum count, objects across strata (Reviewer_X4zp, Reviewer_1vpo)
No qualitative results and no undistortion in the backbone (Reviewer_X4zp); no single-frame baseline (Reviewer_X4zp, Reviewer_1vpo)
Detection valued above segmentation, and the joint task questioned (Reviewer_dNFe)
shared_issues: Incremental novelty over Han et al. and STROBE (A: Reviewer_88yB, Reviewer_ijm6; B: Reviewer_1vpo)
Evaluation on nuScenes only (A: Reviewer_2ez1, Reviewer_88yB; B: Reviewer_X4zp)
Accuracy below full-sweep methods in Figure 5 (A: Reviewer_88yB, Reviewer_ijm6; B: Reviewer_1vpo, Reviewer_dNFe); both committees received the same heavier-backbone table
Unexplained rise in detection mAP with more sectors (A: Reviewer_ijm6; B: Reviewer_X4zp)
Clarity of the method text (A: Reviewer_88yB; B: Reviewer_X4zp, Reviewer_1vpo), though Reviewer_dNFe called it well-written
Uncited warping and undistortion work (A: Reviewer_ijm6, as optional citations; B: Reviewer_1vpo, as a novelty concern)
verdict: A accepted on 6, 7, 6, 6 and B rejected on 5, 5, 5. This is not a different weighting of the same facts: each committee decided on an issue the other never heard. B's Reviewer_dNFe and Reviewer_X4zp tested the paper's motivating claim that polar sectors avoid the memory and compute that cartesian rectangles waste. The paper does not support it. Figure 1 puts PolarStream within about 2 ms of the cartesian Han et al. at every sector count, and no memory figure appears. Polar detection also trails cartesian pillars at full sweep (51.2 vs 52.3 mAP) and at 4 sectors (53.2 vs 54.9). The rebuttal conceded no runtime gain on a V100, showed smaller feature maps only at 8 or more sectors, and told Reviewer_1vpo 'Our major contribution is not polar representation', against the paper's first listed contribution. All B reviewers kept 5, and the AC rejected on this point. No A reviewer raised it; Reviewer_ijm6 restated the efficiency claim as fact. A's doubts were the reimplemented baselines and the gap to full-sweep methods. The rebuttal recast the baselines as a contribution, a promised open streaming benchmark with code. Reviewer_ijm6 called this 'good citizenship', Reviewer_88yB cited the phrase and moved above threshold, and A's two-sentence meta-review repeats the promise. No B reviewer asked about baselines, so B never heard the pledge. Both committees credited the gains over streaming baselines in Table 1, and both sat at the threshold. A's 7 from Reviewer_8rdp is a two-sentence review; without it A still averages 6.0.
candidate_reasons: Motivating claim contradicted by own results

Authors' response to Reviewer_1vpo ('Our major contribution is not polar representation')
